We discuss how emotions, stories and culture shape the way we perceive the world, learn and build a sense of self. data.description: From the rise of ambient intelligence to the changing nature of work and scientific discovery, what might be possible by 2030? What skills will matter most? And how do we decide which problems to solve as our technological capabilities expand?   In this episode of I’ve Got Questions, I sit down with Yossi Matias, VP of Google Research, for a fireside chat about the next frontiers of AI and science, and how the technologies being developed today could reshape our everyday lives.    We explore his vision for the future, the possibilities emerging across disciplines, and what it means to prepare for a world where the boundaries of what’s possible are rapidly expanding. data.description: So... Why Isn't the AI Bubble Popping?  In 2025, OpenAI lost about $1.60 for every $1 it earned just running its business. Yet Big Tech is still on track to spend around $725 billion on AI infrastructure this year alone, and just seven tech giants now make up about a third of the S&P 500, the same index sitting in millions of Americans’ retirement accounts. The risk is already enormous, and we've yet to account for both Anthropic and OpenAI's upcoming IPOs - meaning 2027... could get very, VERY volatile.  On this Episode, We’ll Cover:  - Why Nvidia, Big Tech and the White House are all-in on the AI boom  - How Nvidia became the shovel seller of the AI gold rush  - OpenAI’s losses and the circular financing loop between Nvidia, OpenAI and Oracle  - Why AI IPOs like Anthropic and OpenAI shift the risk onto retail investors  - What South Korea’s KOSPI crash reveals about AI concentration in the S&P 500  ----  Support Our Work: https://www.youtube.com/@MonkeyExplains1999/membership  ----  Sauce - https://pastebin.com/JJyM2DuD  ----  AI Disclosure: I want to be clear about how we create our videos. We're a small team of actual people and all of the visuals you see are hand-drawn.  AI is used ONLY for Dubbing/Narration. Most of the team, including myself are based in South East Asia and English isn't our best language. I personally had negative experiences being bullied for my Singaporean Accent when I worked in the marketing industry. And now, considering the subjects of our videos - this is a way to help protect the identity of everyone working on this channel.  Everything from scripting, jokes, references, editing, and overall creativity, is 100% me and my amazing team of animators and illustrators.
